extracted.intended_audience: Users and programmers of the PARI/GP computer algebra system (GP script authors, mathematicians using PARI libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP functions, parallel constructs, I/O primitives, and GP defaults describing semantics, side‑effects, performance, and recommended usage patterns for writing GP scripts and library code.

rubrics_metrics.name: listput
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert an element into a list at a given position (listput(L, x, n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use listput to insert an element into an occupied cell (not changing the list length) but simpler assignments like list[n] = x can be used to insert at the end. listput runs in O(#L) worst-case (when the list must be reallocated), but O(1) on average across many successive listputs. Library syntax: GEN listput0(GEN list, GEN x, long n). Examples show behavior when inserting at positions within and beyond current length and resulting exceptions when assigning beyond end with direct indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: listsort
rubrics_metrics.description: Sorts a t_LIST in place using the universal comparison function cmp (listsort(L, {flag = 0})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sorting is in-place (faster than vecsort which copies). setsearch may be used on the sorted list since ordering matches sets. If flag != 0, repeated coefficients are suppressed. No return value. Library syntax: void listsort(GEN L, long flag). Examples: listsort(L) on [1,2,4,1,3,-1] gives [-1,1,1,2,3,4].

rubrics_metrics.name: localbitprec
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the real precision to p bits in dynamic scope; computations act as if realbitprecision = p (localbitprec(p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masks realbitprecision in dynamic scope; nested localbitprec statements take precedence. A subroutine called from within localbitprec uses the masked accuracy. Bit precision increments in machine-word steps (e.g., by 64 on typical machines), so requested p may be rounded up to the next multiple of the machine step. Use instead of changing global realbitprecision; mixing localbitprec with default(realbitprecision,...) can yield surprising results. Library syntax documented; examples show effects on bitprecision(1.0) and on Pi computation. Consider using localprec/localbitprec rather than changing global defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: localprec
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the real precision to p decimal digits in dynamic scope; computations act as if realprecision = p (localprec(p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masks realprecision in dynamic scope; nested localprec statements take precedence; subroutines see masked accuracy. Changing realprecision directly in programs is deprecated in favor of localprec. Mixing localprec and default(realprecision,...) yields surprising behaviour: realprecision is ignored within localprec scope and not restored to original value on exit. Examples show precision(1.) and effect on Pi. Library and semantic notes provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: mapdelete
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove a key x from the domain of map M (mapdelete(M, x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: M = Map(["a",1; "b",3; "c",7]); mapdelete(M,"b"); Mat(M) then shows remaining pairs. Library syntax: void mapdelete(GEN M, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mapget
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the image/value associated to key x in map M (mapget(M, x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises an exception when the key is not present in M (example shows top-level exception text). Example: M=Map(["a",23;"b",43]); mapget(M,"a") -> 23. Library syntax: GEN mapget(GEN M, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mapisdefined
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether key x has an image in map M; optional &z returns the image if present (mapisdefined(M, x, {&z})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns 1 (true) if defined, 0 otherwise. If third argument provided, sets z to the image. Examples include using mapisdefined in loops to print cubes mod N. Library syntax: GEN mapisdefined(GEN M, GEN x, GEN *z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: mapput
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate key x to value y in map M (mapput(M, x, y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value y can then be retrieved with mapget. Examples show mixed-type keys and retrieval. Library syntax: void mapput(GEN M, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: print
rubrics_metrics.description: Output arguments in raw format followed by a newline (print({str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments converted to strings following Section 2.9 rules. Example: print(matid(2)) prints [1, 0; 0, 1] in raw format. For pretty matrix format use printp. Behavior contrasted with print1 which omits the trailing newline.

rubrics_metrics.name: print1
rubrics_metrics.description: Output arguments in raw format without a trailing newline (print1({str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may embed newlines within strings via \n. Arguments converted per Section 2.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: printf
rubrics_metrics.description: C-style formatted printing: printf(fmt, {x}*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format string composed of ordinary characters and conversion specifications (% with optional flags, field width, precision, length modifier, and conversion specifier). Flags supported: #, 0, -, ' ' (space), +. Field width can be numeric or *, precision as .n or .*. Length modifiers are ignored in gp (listed for completeness). Conversion specifiers: d,i,o,u,x,X,p,e,E,f,F,g,G,c,s,%, with detailed behavior for each (e.g., e/E style, f style, g/G style rules, s maximum characters behavior). Examples illustrate field widths, padding, sign, vector/matrix recursive application, and mixed formatting. Technical notes list deviations from C89/C99: missing precision uses current realprecision (not 6); exponent formatting differs (no +, exponent digits variable), f may switch to e if exponent >= precision, g/G do not remove trailing zeros nor trailing decimal point, and 0 printed specially as 0.Eexp. All numerical conversions apply recursively to vectors/matrices. Examples and edge-cases shown. Use of printf with vectors/matrices is demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: printp
rubrics_metrics.description: Output arguments in prettymatrix format followed by a newline (printp({str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments converted to strings following Section 2.9. Example contrasts from print: printp(matid(2)) prints in a pretty matrix layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: printsep
rubrics_metrics.description: Output arguments separated by sep and ending with a newline (printsep(sep, {str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments converted per Section 2.9. Example: printsep(":", 1,2,3,4) -> 1:2:3:4.

rubrics_metrics.name: printsep1
rubrics_metrics.description: Output arguments separated by sep without ending newline (printsep1(sep, {str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for composing lines piecemeal. Example: printsep1(":",1,2,3,4); print("|") -> 1:2:3:4|

rubrics_metrics.name: printtex
rubrics_metrics.description: Output arguments in TeX format for inclusion in TeX manuscripts (printtex({str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments converted to TeX strings per Section 2.9. Output goes to standard output; to write to a file use writetex or enable log default and printtex(result).

rubrics_metrics.name: quit
rubrics_metrics.description: Exit gp returning an integer exit status to the system (quit({status = 0})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System sees status mod 256; non-zero normally indicates abnormal termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: read
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and evaluate a file (read({filename})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filename omitted, re-reads last file fed into gp. Return value is result of last expression evaluated. If reading a GP binary file, file is loaded and last object returned. Avoid allocatemem statements in files (leave read instructions by themselves). Variants/read alternatives: readvec (read whole file), fileopen/fileread/filereadstr for line-at-a-time. Library syntax: GEN gp_read_file(const char *filename).

rubrics_metrics.name: readstr
rubrics_metrics.description: Read file and return a vector of GP strings, each a line (readstr({filename})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filename omitted, re-reads last file fed into gp. Library syntax: GEN readstr(const char *filename).

rubrics_metrics.name: readvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Read file and return a vector whose components are the evaluation of instruction sequences in the file (readvec({filename})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sequence usually one line; returns evaluated results. Example: file containing lines 1,2,3 leads to readvec -> [1,2,3]. Library syntax: GEN gp_readvec_file(const char *filename). Underlying stream interface GEN gp_readvec_stream(FILE *f) more flexible.

rubrics_metrics.name: select
rubrics_metrics.description: Select elements x of vector/list A such that f(x) is non-zero (select(f, A, {flag = 0})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default returns elements; if flag=1 returns indices (indirect selection). Applies to matrices selecting columns. Shortcuts with set-notation [g(x) | x <- v, f(x)] and [x | x <- v, f(x)]. Example selectors: primes from vector, selecting non-zero entries, invertibles(N) defined via select. Library syntax: genselect(void *E, long (*fun)(void*,GEN), GEN a) and genindexselect for flag=1. To remove entries use negation of f.

rubrics_metrics.name: self
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the calling function or closure as a t_CLOSURE to enable anonymous recursion (self()).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (n->if(n==0,1,n*self()(n-1)))(5) -> 120. Library syntax: GEN pari_self().

rubrics_metrics.name: setrand
rubrics_metrics.description: Reseed the random number generator deterministically using seed n (setrand(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed is a small positive integer 0 < n < 2^64. All sessions start with implicit setrand(1) so resetting to 1 replays session. Use setrand(getwalltime()) or /dev/urandom for varying seeds. For debugging, record/getrand() state (huge integer) and later setrand(state) to replay exact computations. Library syntax: void setrand(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: system
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute an external system command and write its output to standard output (system(str)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This calls the C system command; command output goes to standard output and won't get into your gp log file. Library syntax: void gpsystem(const char *str).

rubrics_metrics.name: trap (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete error trapping construct: trap({e}, {rec}, seq) evaluates seq and traps runtime error e, executing rec on error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use iferr instead (nicer and more powerful). trap evaluates seq up to the error point and executes recovery sequence in the same context—does not undo side-effects already performed. Examples demonstrate trapping division-by-zero and caution about partial side-effects. The interface currently recognizes a set of named exceptions (e_ALARM, e_ARCH, e_STACK, e_INV, e_IMPL, e_OVERFLOW, e_SYNTAX, e_MISC, e_TYPE, e_USER) and will expand in future. Library syntax: GEN trap0(const char *e = NULL, GEN rec = NULL, GEN seq = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: type
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the internal type name of a PARI object x as a string (type(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful only under gp; e.g. type(1) returns "t_INT". Use metacommand \t to check names. Library syntax: GEN type0(GEN x). The macro typ returns a long (symbolic t_* value) which may be simpler to match.

rubrics_metrics.name: uninline
rubrics_metrics.description: Exit the scope of all current inline variables (uninline()).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked experimental in the doc; no extensive guidance provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: version
rubrics_metrics.description: Return current PARI version as a vector [major, minor, patchlevel] and optional extra development components (version()).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for conditional code; lex() offers a way to compare version vectors robustly even when length differs. Example: if (lex(version(), [2,3,5]) >= 0, ... ). Development versions may include additional components (commit count, git hash). Example code provided to format version numbers for introductory message. Library syntax: GEN pari_version().

rubrics_metrics.name: warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Emit a user warning and the provided message list (warning({str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If colors enabled, warning will be colorized to stand out. Example usage: warning(n, " is very large, this might take a while.").

rubrics_metrics.name: whatnow
rubrics_metrics.description: Map old GP function names (present in older GP versions) to new names/syntax (whatnow(key)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a function changed name or syntax since version 1.39.15, whatnow reports the new syntax and description; if the function did not change it reports so; if removed, reports that it no longer exists and may hint at closest equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: write
rubrics_metrics.description: Append arguments (converted to strings) with a trailing newline to filename (write(filename, {str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level write is expensive for many consecutive writes because it cannot use buffering. For efficiency use fileopen/filewrite/fileclose low-level interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: write1
rubrics_metrics.description: Append arguments without a trailing newline to filename (write1(filename, {str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same semantics as print1 vs print.

rubrics_metrics.name: writebin
rubrics_metrics.description: Write an object x in binary format to filename (writebin(filename, {x})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary format stores exact internal structure and is faster to save/load than textual write. If x is omitted, saves all user variables with names; reading such a file restores variables with original names and priorities. Binary files include a magic number and can be gzip-compressed (.gz). Current implementation is architecture-dependent and not guaranteed compatible with future versions — do not use for long-term storage; binary files are larger and harder to compress than text. Installed functions and history objects cannot be saved. Library syntax: void gpwritebin(const char *filename, GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: writetex
rubrics_metrics.description: Append arguments in TeX format to filename (writetex(filename, {str}*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same as write but the arguments are converted to TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: parapply
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel evaluation of closure f on elements of x (parapply(f, x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function f must not access global variables or variables declared with local(); it must be free of side-effects. Useful for applying expensive arithmetic/maths functions (examples: factoring or elliptic-curve computations over lists of arguments). Library syntax: GEN parapply(GEN f, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: pareval
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel evaluation of a vector of closures (pareval(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closures must be arity 0, must not access global variables or variables declared with local, and must be free of side-effects. Library syntax: GEN pareval(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: parfor
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel for-loop: evaluate expr1 for formal argument i from a to b in parallel; optional r and expr2 allow sequential processing of results (parfor(i = a, {b}, expr1, {r}, {expr2})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computations of expr1 are started in increasing order of i but completion order may differ; expr2 is evaluated sequentially on each result r as it becomes available. The sequential evaluation of expr2 ensures no concurrent modification of shared variables (e.g., accumulating into s). expr2 may exit loop via break/next/return; semantics given for early exits: if expr2 exits for i = c, expr1 and expr2 continue for all i < c, and the return value corresponds to smallest i causing interruption. Using side-effects in expr2 may lead to undefined behaviour because exact number of expr2 evaluations is nondeterministic. Examples: parfor to compute sum of squares by computing squares in parallel then sequentially accumulating; parallel nextprime example. The expression expr1 must be free of side-effects that conflict with parallel evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: parforprime
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel loop over primes only: behaves as parfor but iterates p through primes from a to b (parforprime(p = a, {b}, expr1, {r}, {expr2})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same parallel and exit semantics as parfor; expr2 may exit loop with break/next/return with similar consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: parforvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel evaluation over values generated by forvec: parforvec(X = v, expr1, {j}, {expr2}, {flag}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates expr2 (dependent on X and j) for X produced by forvec in random order computed in parallel; expr2 may exit using break/next/return but will still be evaluated for remaining values less than current one unless a subsequent exit occurs. Intended for parallel processing of collections generated by forvec.

rubrics_metrics.name: parselect
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel selection of elements of A according to selection function f (parselect(f, A, {flag = 0})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1 return indices (indirect selection). The function f must not access global variables or local variables and must be free of side-effects. Library syntax: GEN parselect(GEN f, GEN A, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: parsum
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel sum of expression expr evaluated for i from a to b, initialized at x (parsum(i = a, b, expr, {x})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of expr are done in parallel in random order; expr must not access global variables or local variables and must be free of side-effects. Example: count of primes among first N Mersenne numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: parvector
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel vector construction: as vector(N,i,expr) but expr evaluated in parallel (parvector(N, i, expr)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expression expr must not access global variables or variables declared with local, and must be free of side-effects. Example: computing class numbers in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: TeXstyle
rubrics_metrics.description: TeXstyle default controls less-rigid TeX formatting bits for logfile output (TeXstyle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bits: 2 = insert \right/\left pairs where appropriate; 4 = insert discretionary breaks in polynomials to improve line breaks. Default value is 0. Only relevant when log = 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: breakloop
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable or disable 'break loop' debugging mode (breakloop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 1 if running interactive gp, and 0 otherwise. See Section 2.10.3 for debugging details.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: colors
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls color palette used by gp in capable terminals; value is a string describing up to seven items mapping to output categories (colors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted items: 'no', integer 0-15, or triple [fg,bg,attr] where attr 0 default, 1 bold, 4 underline. Items correspond to error messages, history numbers, prompt, input line, output, help messages, timer (seven categories). k < 7 implies remaining assumed 'no'. Preset values darkbg, lightbg, boldfg available. Incompatible with PariEmacs (will fail silently); customize in PariEmacs instead. Default value is "" (no colors). Examples illustrate setting default(colors, "9, 5, no, no, 4").

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: compatible
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete default; currently no-op (compatible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented as obsolete and retained for compatibility only.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: datadir
rubrics_metrics.description: Directory name containing optional data files used by gp (datadir).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes packages such as elldata, galdata, galpol, seadata. Default is /usr/local/share/pari or the Configure override --datadir=.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: debug
rubrics_metrics.description: General debugging level: extra messages printed when non-zero (debug).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0 (no debugging). See \g for details on interactive debugging commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: debugfiles
rubrics_metrics.description: File usage debugging level (debugfiles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-zero, gp will print information on file descriptors in use from PARI's point of view (see \gf). Default 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: debugmem
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory debugging verbosity level (debugmem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: >0 notify when parisize changes; >1 indicate important garbage collection and function; >2 indicate creation/destruction of 'blocks' (very verbose). Important note: on debugging builds and debugmem >1 gp will print stack usage changes by 1 MByte regularly; disabled on non-debugging builds because of performance penalty. Default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: echo
rubrics_metrics.description: Echo mode for commands (echo = 0,1,2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 0 off (default), 1 on (cleaned input reprinted before execution: whitespace/comments removed and multiline input united), 2 on raw (input reprinted as-is). Useful when reading files with \r or read; test files use echo on during build tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: factor_add_primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle whether integer factorization machinery calls addprimes on large prime factors found during factorization (factor add primes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If on (1), primes larger than 2^24 found during factorization are added to an internal table and tried first in subsequent factorizations; allows recovery of factors after interruption. Downside: huge unrelated addprimes tables slow down arithmetic functions relying on factorization; use removeprimes to clear table. Default is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: factor_proven
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle whether integer factorization outputs are proven primes (factor proven).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If on (1), perform primality proofs for each factor so dependent results are fully proven. Default is 0. Does not affect explicitly requested partial factorizations or entries in addprimes private table (which are included as is without testing).

rubrics_metrics.name: GP default: format
rubrics_metrics.description: Default printing format of real numbers specified as x.n where x in {e,f,g} conversion style and n precision (format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects how real numbers are printed: e for scientific with explicit exponent (e.g., 3.3E-5), f for fixed, g for general style. The chunk documents that format is of the form x.n and begins description for style e; other styles handled similarly earlier in printf description. This default influences printed representation of reals in gp.
